head: bd556e58ce91797a3b0b1abf11dfd9f93cae07ec
summary: I fixed O-015 (review finding m1) in two places. In StartupHook.cs, Act now runs in its own try/catch inside the dispatcher callback. When one of the app's handlers throws during the press (OnCancel for stop, OnClosing for close), the hook logs a 'rethrown' line and re-raises the exception on the dispatcher with ExceptionDispatchInfo and BeginInvoke(Send). App.DispatcherUnhandledException then handles it, as it would from a real press, instead of Run's catch recording it as the hook's failure. In WindowCases.ps1, CheckActed now fails when a 'refused' line follows the 'acted' line. The hooked cases return before the exit-code and report checks, so a hook that failed after acting can no longer print 'exit code ok'. Two new opt-in mutants in WindowMutants.ps1 prove both halves. CancelThrows: OnCancel throws, the app exits 70 with no report, and C-006 fails only on the exit code and the missing report. HookFailsAfterActing: C-006 fails only on the new check. WindowCases -Case All (15 cases), WindowMutants -Mutant All (8 mutants), the Core tests (120/120) and rules-parity all passed.

files.why: O-015. Act is wrapped in try/catch inside the Invoke callback. On an exception the hook logs 'rethrown mode=<m> reason=<type>: <message>' and re-raises it with ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture plus Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(DispatcherPriority.Send, fault.Throw), so the app's DispatcherUnhandledException sees it. `acted = true` now comes after the try/catch. The log-contract remarks document the new 'rethrown' line. The hook still never exits, shuts down or sets an exit code, and the three architecture rules still match nothing.

O-015. CheckActed now also checks for any 'refused' line after the 'acted' line ('the hook did not fail after it acted'). The existing early return in C-006, C-012 and O-016 then stops the case before the exit code or the report is read. A 'rethrown' line is not counted as the hook failing.

Adds the CancelThrows mutant (OnCancel throws) and the HookFailsAfterActing mutant (the hook throws after pressing Stop) as runnable proof of the fix. Renamed AppMutants and Test-AppMutant to CaseMutants and Test-CaseMutant, because one mutant now edits the hook. Fail is now an ordered list of the case's FAIL lines, and a new optional Expect lists other lines the run must show. Both new mutants are in -Mutant All.

obligations.how: Both parts of the finding's fix are in. (1) StartupHook.cs catches exceptions from Act inside the Invoke callback, logs 'rethrown', and re-posts them with ExceptionDispatchInfo.Capture(e) and app.Dispatcher.BeginInvoke(DispatcherPriority.Send, new Action(fault.Throw)). (2) CheckActed fails on any 'refused' line after the 'acted' line. Measured with WindowMutants.ps1 -Mutant CancelThrows, the reviewer's own mutant (OnCancel throws): the log now reads 'acted' then 'rethrown mode=stop reason=InvalidOperationException: mutant: OnCancel threw'. The app exited 70 with no report, as a real click would, and C-006 failed only on 'exit code' (expected '0', actual '70') and 'a report was written'. The hook's own checks passed. Before the fix the reviewer saw exit 0 and a Finished report. -Mutant HookFailsAfterActing (the hook throws after pressing, and the app still ends Stopped with exit 0 and a report) now fails C-006 only on 'the hook did not fail after it acted'. The old CheckActed would have let that run pass. Both mutants passed on their own and inside -Mutant All.

deviations: The FSA_HOOK_LOG contract gains one line kind: 'rethrown mode=<m> reason=<text>', meaning the app's own handler threw during the press and the exception was handed back to the app. I did not log it as 'refused'. The new CheckActed rule fails on 'refused' after 'acted', so logging it that way would fail any case about a handler fault on the hook's check, which is exactly the problem the finding describes. 'refused' still means only that the hook itself did not or could not act.
follow_ups: The tree slice's click and expand modes should keep the same shape: call the app's handler inside a try/catch in the dispatcher callback and re-raise with ExceptionDispatchInfo. Otherwise a handler fault there would again be recorded as the hook's own failure.

tests.command: pwsh -NoProfile -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File eng/dotnet.ps1 build tests/window/FsaWindowHook/FsaWindowHook.csproj -c Release -o artifacts/window-hook
tests.note: 0 warnings, 0 errors after the O-015 change.
Log: 'acted' then 'rethrown ... mutant: OnCancel threw'. The app exited 70 with no report. C-006 failed on exactly 'exit code' and 'a report was written'. Run twice: alone and inside All.
C-006 failed only on 'the hook did not fail after it acted'. Run twice: alone and inside All.
15 cases in 152 s with the fixed hook and CheckActed.
All 8 mutants passed, including the 6 from attempt 1 unchanged, in about 273 s. No scratch copies or FsAnalyser.App processes were left behind.
120/120. InteropLivesOnlyInNative still holds: there is no DllImport in the hook.
AGREE, 7 facts. A grep of the SL-033 must_not_match patterns and (Library|Dll)Import over tests/window/FsaWindowHook found no matches.
